title: Neural Compression of Long ADMM Trajectory for Multiparametric Quadratic Program
claim: A model is trained offline without labels, then at inference a learned warm start plus a few refinement iterations is checked against a residual certificate.
layout: 2 stacked rows (training, inference), left-to-right flow, shared problem box feeding both
description: The figure has two horizontal rounded panels, one stacked above the other. A green box on the left holds the quadratic program (min 0.5xᵀQx + q(p)ᵀx s.t. Ax ≥ c(p)). Thick black arrows lead from it into both panels. The top panel has an orange 'Offline Training Phase' banner. It runs from sampled parameters through a neural-network icon (MLP), a light-blue 'K layers low-dimensional ADMM-ReLU' box, and a purple box with the residual loss J, to a peach 'minimize loss until J ≤ ε_off' box. The bottom panel has a blue 'Online Inference Phase' banner. It shows batch instances going through the same MLP and ADMM-ReLU blocks into a diamond 'Check J ≤ ε_on'. caption: Architecture of TQPNet based on the hybrid MLP(ReLU)-ADMM(ReLU) neural network.
abstract: Solving large-scale multiparametric quadratic programs (mpQPs) in real time often requires thousands of iterative optimization updates, creating a major computational bottleneck in model predictive control and learning-enabled systems. This paper proposes TQPNet, a self-supervised neural compression framework that learns to compress long ADMM optimization trajectories into a compact neural warm start followed by a few refinement iterations. We derive a low-dimensional ADMM scheme operating on the primal-dual variables $(x,Î²)$ and show that its iteration admits an equivalent ReLU-layer representation, termed ADMM(ReLU). Building on this insight, TQPNet combines a multilayer perceptron with ReLU activations (MLP(ReLU)) and a small number of unrolled ADMM(ReLU) refinement layers. The network is trained offline using an optimality-condition-informed residual loss, eliminating the need for solver-generated labels. The proposed residual-based framework enables both self-supervised training and online solution certification through adaptive ADMM(ReLU) refinement. Experiments on large-scale mpQPs and real-time MPC applications demonstrate that TQPNet achieves high accuracy, strong generalization, and substantially faster inference than conventional optimization-based methods.
